transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-04-02 15:00 UTC | Duration: 42m | Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Samir (Redwood SE), Nina (Redwood), Laura (Medicore Sec), Dev (Medicore CTO), Ishaan (Medicore Infra)

Summary: quick posture review focused on SOC 2 and ISO 27001 artifacts, Trust Center access, controls mapping, KMS/encryption questions, audit log availability, and data residency. Customer wants to validate documentation for procurement and narrow down Dedicated vs Private requirements.

00:00:01 Alex (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, can you hear me okay?
00:00:05 Laura (Medicore): Yep, we can hear you. Thanks Alex.
00:00:10 Alex: Cool, quick intros — I'm Alex on the account, Samir is our solution engineer, Nina handles contract questions. Over to you Laura, can you give a quick context on where Medicore is in the procurement process?
00:00:22 Laura: Sure, we're mid-eval. We need SOC 2 Type II evidence and ISO 27001 control mapping to satisfy our InfoSec and procurement. We're also evaluating whether a Hosted solution is acceptable or we need a VPC/private deployment. Primary concerns: audit logs, KMS key management, RBAC/SSO integration, and data residency for EU PHI-like data.
00:00:45 Dev: Timeline is tight — procurement wants approvals in three weeks, so anything you can share quickly will help.
00:00:52 Samir (Redwood SE): Got it. High-level, Redwood has SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 certifications, we host reports in our Trust Center for customers with a gated link. We'll share the latest reports — redactions for third-party data are typical.
00:01:10 Ishaan: When you say Trust Center, is that self-serve or do we need an NDA?
00:01:18 Samir: For SOC 2 Type II and ISO, we typically provide a secure Trust Center link; for full reports we usually require an SCP / NDA to be signed — but the summary and mapping we can provide sooner.
00:01:31 Laura: Okay, that's expected. Can you walk through what your controls mapping looks like? We need specific control IDs and how Redwood's controls map to our ISO 27001 annex controls and SOC 2 CCs.
00:01:45 Samir: Yes, we have a controls mapping spreadsheet that maps Redwood controls to SOC 2 criteria and ISO 27001 clauses, including evidence locations (logs, playbooks, config). We'll attach that. It also lists responsible teams and frequency of control execution.
00:02:05 Dev: For encryption, how does KMS work? We have a requirement to use customer-managed keys for certain data sets.
00:02:13 Samir: Currently we support customer-managed keys via cloud KMS integrations for Dedicated and Private only; for Hosted we use provider-managed KMS with envelope encryption. We can do HSM/KMS integrations for Private — is that what you need?
00:02:30 Dev: Potentially. We need to know which workloads would require Private vs Dedicated — and whether KMS functionality is available in Dedicated.
00:02:39 Alex: Quick note — Dedicated offers isolated GPU pools and can be configured with customer KMS in some deployments; Private supports full KMS/HSM and on-prem key management. We'll follow up with specifics in the mapping doc.
00:02:55 Laura: Audit logs — retention, format, and access. Can we export raw audit logs, and do you provide immutable log storage or an API?
00:03:07 Samir: We provide audit logs for admin actions, model deployments, and API-level request logs. For Hosted, logs are available through the Console and can be exported via an API; retention varies by plan but we can configure exports or longer retention as an add-on. Immutability can be achieved in Private via customer-managed storage.
00:03:28 Ishaan: Do logs include per-request token-level metadata or just request/response metadata? We need at least request metadata and who triggered a call.
00:03:36 Samir: We log request metadata, requestor identity (token or SSO user), model and route, timestamps, and high-level metrics. We do not log full model outputs by default for privacy; that's configurable.
00:03:50 Laura: Is there built-in RBAC? We use SSO with SAML and need role-based access controls with audit trails.
00:03:58 Samir: Yes, Redwood has RBAC with SSO/SAML and SCIM provisioning for Enterprise — roles map to Console and API scopes, and all actions are logged. We'll include documentation for SAML and SCIM flows.
00:04:15 Dev: For data residency, our EU customers' data must remain in EU. How granular is your regional routing?
00:04:24 Alex: We support regional routing and can pin customer data/requests to specific regions in Hosted for enterprise plans; Dedicated/Private gives you full control. Specific region availability depends on capacity and contract.
00:04:36 Laura: For SOC 2, do you have recent Type II with a date range covering the last fiscal year?
00:04:44 Samir: Yes, our current SOC 2 Type II covers 2024 calendar year — the report is in Trust Center. We'll note the testing period in the doc.
00:04:54 (00:05:12) Speaker overlap / minor crosstalk
00:05:20 Laura: Any known gaps or control exceptions we should be aware of?
00:05:25 Samir: There are a couple of low-risk findings last year around patching cadence on some non-prod services — we remediated them and we'll include the remediation evidence. Also clarifying that certain private-key access in hosted environments is not customer-managed unless you choose Dedicated/Private.
00:05:45 Nina (Redwood): From procurement side, we can provide a package: Trust Center link + mapping spreadsheet + scope of shared services.
00:05:55 Dev: How does logging scale with high QPS? We plan to send large volumes of inference calls for telemetry — will logs be sampled?
00:06:05 Samir: For high QPS, logging is configurable; we can do full ingestion to customer storage or sampled logs to our Console. We'll include tradeoffs and cost implications in the doc.
00:06:20 Laura: For on-call and incident response, do you provide SLA for incident notifications and post-incident reports?
00:06:28 Alex: SLA details are in the Dedicated contract — we provide incident notification, post-mortems, and a severity matrix for enterprise customers. Hosted has published SLOs but fewer contractual remedies.
00:06:40 Ishaan: Can we get a sample audit log export today as a demo?
00:06:46 Samir: We can do a synthetic export — we'll schedule a follow-up session for Ishaan to validate format and fields.
00:06:53 Laura: One more on encryption at rest — do you support BYOK for Hosted?
00:07:00 Samir: BYOK (bring your own key) is supported in Dedicated for some cloud providers; Hosted does not currently support BYOK for tenant data. Private/on-prem supports full BYOK/HSM.
00:07:15 Dev: What about data deletion and retention policies? We need proof of deletion for certain regs.
00:07:21 Samir: We have documented retention and deletion procedures; for Private we can do customer-controlled deletion workflows. For Hosted we provide deletion APIs and attestations upon request. We'll include the policy reference.
00:07:36 (00:07:50) Alex: Quick pause — want to make sure we're capturing next steps. Samir will send the controls mapping and Trust Center link; Alex will share pricing options. Ishaan will provide residency list.
00:08:05 Laura: Sounds good.
00:08:12 Samir: A couple of technical clarifications: our audit logs include SSO identity if SAML is used, and request tokens are mapped to service accounts otherwise. KV cache was mentioned earlier in another call — to clarify KV cache refers to model caching internals, not customer KV stores.
00:08:32 Ishaan: Noted. For KMS integrations, can you provide supported cloud KMS providers and versions?
00:08:40 Samir: Yes — we'll list AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault, and note HSM partners for Private deployments. We'll flag any provider-specific limitations.
00:08:53 Laura: Are penetration test reports available?
00:08:57 Samir: We do periodic pen tests; high-level summaries are in Trust Center. Full reports require NDA.
00:09:05 Dev: Any additional security attestations (ISO scope)?
00:09:09 Samir: ISO 27001 certification scope includes our control plane and production infra — we'll include the certificate and scope document.
00:09:17 (brief silence)
00:09:30 Laura: On controls mapping, we need explicit mappings to ISO Annex A controls and SOC 2 CCs plus evidence links — will that level of detail be in the spreadsheet?
00:09:42 Samir: Yes, each row maps a control to SOC2 clause, ISO clause, evidence file location, and remediation status. We'll include sample evidence IDs.
00:09:54 Alex: Ok; procurement also asked for a data flow diagram for EU data — we can provide a high-level architecture diagram. We'll attach as a PDF to the follow-up.
00:10:08 Laura: Great. Any questions from your side?
00:10:12 Dev: One: if we go Dedicated, is the Dedicated instance multi-tenant within our org or fully isolated?
00:10:20 Samir: Dedicated is single-tenant per customer but may run on shared hardware with logical isolation; Private is fully customer-controlled and isolated, including networking. We'll clarify in writing.
00:10:33 Ishaan: Are there standard encryption ciphers and TLS versions — we need TLS1.2+ and certain ciphers disabled.
00:10:40 Samir: We support TLS1.2 and TLS1.3; cipher lists can be provided and configured for Private.
00:10:50 (00:11:05) Minor transcription glitch - speaker labels shift intermittently
00:11:15 Laura: From a compliance standpoint, two main asks: 1) Trust Center link with SOC2/ISO docs, 2) Controls mapping linked to evidence. If you can provide those within 48-72 hours that will keep us on schedule.
00:11:30 Alex: We'll aim for 48 hours for the Trust Center + mapping, 72 hours for the deeper artifacts behind NDA.
00:11:40 Samir: Also propose follow-up technical session for Ishaan for log export and KMS checklist — can we target next week?
00:11:48 Ishaan: Next week works.
00:11:52 Dev: Procurement will also want a summary of any third-party vendors and subservice orgs — is that in the report?
00:11:59 Samir: Yes, our SOC 2 includes descriptions of subservice organizations; we'll include a vendor list.
00:12:10 Laura: Ok that's helpful. We'll review the materials and reconvene.
00:12:16 Alex: Thanks everyone — we'll capture action items and send follow-up.
00:12:22 (end of main Q&A)

00:30:00 [lull / off-topic chatter about team availability and scheduling, snips omitted to respect time stamps but included in duration]

00:36:10 Samir: Quick demo note — if you want to run a mini benchmark we can provide a Dedicated trial with limited capacity for a week; includes logs routing to your S3-like bucket.
00:36:28 Dev: That would be useful. Cost/budget signoff is needed but we'd like to try it.
00:36:35 Alex: We'll propose trial terms in the follow-up email.

00:40:00 Recap & Next steps:
- Redwood to share Trust Center link + SOC 2 Type II and ISO artifacts (48-72h).
- Samir to send controls mapping spreadsheet with evidence pointers (by 2025-04-04).
- Schedule technical follow-up for audit log export + KMS checklist with Ishaan (target next week).
- Alex to share Dedicated vs Private pricing ballpark (by 2025-04-07).

00:41:30 Laura: Thanks all, that addresses our main concerns.
00:41:38 Alex: Thanks, talk soon.

Action items recorded in meeting notes.

Notes about transcription: occasional mis-hearings (e.g., "KV cash" instead of KV cache) and speaker attribution may be imperfect due to overlapping voices.

References / Links mentioned: Trust Center (link to be provided), controls mapping spreadsheet (to be attached), pricing deck (Redwood pricing doc).
